question: What changes in your card or bank contract when your bank is sold?
answer: The library follows 6 bank sales and card-program moves since April 1, 2025 (Ally / Merrick, Capital One / Discover, Goldman, Fifth Third, Bilt / Column, PNC). In each, the brand, card number or app stays while the legal bank behind it changes, and the customer's new terms arrive on a separate, later clock; 2 conversions (Fifth Third, Goldman) have no customer contract published yet.

sections.title: Deal by deal
sections.sub: The acquired bank or card program appears under its new owner, with its own legal name.

groups.label: Ally / Merrick

items.key: fine:2025-04-01:ally s card book closes on car
items.title: Ally's card book closes on CardWorks; Merrick becomes the bank
items.sub: 2025-04-01 · Ally Financial; CardWorks; Merrick Bank; Ollo
kv: $2.3 billion of receivables and 1.3 million active cardholders change hands. Merrick Bank becomes the issuing bank and the entity that reports the customer to the credit bureaus; Ollo becomes the servicing interface. Ally says the promotional APR, credit line, benefits and due date all stay the same, and the account history, alerts, paperless settings, scheduled payments and autopay carry over. The card number even survives — only the expiration and CVV change. Everything the customer can see was engineered to hold still.
Ally Financial; CardWorks; Merrick Bank; Ollo

groups.note: Legal entities involved: Ally Financial; CardWorks; Merrick Bank; Ollo.

groups.label: Capital One / Discover

items.title: Discover Bank merges into Capital One, N.A.
kv: The bank named Discover ceases to exist. The word "Discover" does not. The brand, the account number, the rewards and the interface all remain; the agreements become agreements with Capital One, N.A. Governing law moves from Delaware to Virginia — a fact that comes from the cardmember agreement itself, not, as the source packet stated, from the merger FAQ.

items.title: "Discover" is redefined to mean Capital One
kv: The post-merger cardmember agreement opens by defining its terms: "'We,' 'us,' 'our,' and 'Discover' refer to Capital One, N.A., the issuer of your Card." The old Discover arbitration architecture largely survives inside the new bank — individual AAA arbitration, class waiver, thirty-day mailed opt-out, survival after sale or assignment. One legal bank now carries two visibly different inherited contract families. The merger did not harmonize them.

groups.note: Legal entities involved: Discover Bank; Capital One, N.A..

groups.label: Goldman

items.key: fine:2026-01-07:goldman hands apple card to ch
items.title: Goldman hands Apple Card to Chase; no customer paper exists
items.sub: 2026-01-07 · Goldman Sachs Bank USA; Apple; JPMorgan Chase
kv: Goldman and Chase announce the transition of the Apple Card program — more than $20 billion of balances, expected to move without customer reapplication, Mastercard staying as the network, account data transferring. Expected timing is roughly twenty-four months. Goldman remains the issuer throughout. No Chase customer agreement, privacy notice, assignment notice or change-in-terms package has been issued. The corporate sale and the consumer contract run on different clocks, and the customer's clock has not started.
Goldman Sachs Bank USA; Apple; JPMorgan Chase

items.title: Apple Card's customer contract, whenever it comes
items.sub: 2028-01 · JPMorgan Chase; Goldman Sachs Bank USA; Apple
kv: Roughly twenty-four months from the January 2026 announcement. More than $20 billion of balances expected to move without reapplication. Apple says the details will arrive closer to transition.
JPMorgan Chase; Goldman Sachs Bank USA; Apple

groups.note: Legal entities involved: Goldman Sachs Bank USA; Apple; JPMorgan Chase.

groups.label: Fifth Third

items.title: Comerica becomes a division of Fifth Third
items.sub: 2026-02-01 · Fifth Third Bank, N.A.; Comerica Bank; Fifth Third Bancorp
kv: The merger closes. Fifth Third Bank, N.A. is the surviving bank and becomes the counterparty on existing Comerica swaps. Comerica-branded systems, branches and customer-facing materials remain through conversion — "Comerica Bank, a division of Fifth Third Bank, N.A." Deposits held at the two banks immediately before closing stay separately insured for at least six months. The account mapping, fee comparison, arbitration notice and digital-migration booklet are not yet public.
Fifth Third Bank, N.A.; Comerica Bank; Fifth Third Bancorp

items.title: Fifth Third's Comerica conversion
items.sub: 2026-12 · Fifth Third Bank, N.A.; Comerica Bank
kv: Full customer conversion is scheduled for later in 2026. The account-mapping table, the fee comparison, the arbitration notice and the digital-migration booklet all arrive then. Fifth Third's Federal Reserve submission says consumer checking and savings will be mapped to Fifth Third equivalents and revised terms delivered before conversion. Until then, "Comerica" still appears on the interface of a bank that is already legally Fifth Third.
Fifth Third Bank, N.A.; Comerica Bank

groups.note: Legal entities involved: Fifth Third Bank, N.A.; Comerica Bank; Fifth Third Bancorp.

groups.label: Bilt / Column

items.key: fine:2026-02-07:the bilt card splits into thre
items.title: The Bilt card splits into three companies
items.sub: 2026-02-07 · Bilt; Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.; Column N.A.; Cardless Inc.
kv: Legacy Bilt cards were usable through February 6. Customers who chose "Bilt 2.0" opened a new credit account with Column N.A., serviced by Cardless — while keeping the card number, the autopay and the saved merchant credentials, so that the change was nearly invisible at the point of use. A Wells balance moved only by an optional "Special Transfer," which the new agreement treats as a purchase and excludes from both the introductory APR and new-card rewards. Customers who kept the Wells account had it converted to a Wells Fargo Autograph. The new Column agreement carries its own forty-five-day opt-out and reaches Column, Cardless, servicers, agents, affiliates, assignees, successors, related merchants and collectors.
Bilt; Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.; Column N.A.; Cardless Inc.

groups.note: Legal entities involved: Bilt; Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.; Column N.A.; Cardless Inc..

groups.label: PNC

items.title: PNC converts FirstBank, and the opt-outs do not survive
kv: Systems convert June 19–21. FirstBank customers' opt-outs from discretionary overdraft payment — for checks, automatic bill payments and recurring debit transactions — did not carry over, and PNC states it does not offer an opt-out for that process. Savings and money-market accounts can no longer serve as overdraft-protection accounts. Zelle customers must re-enroll. Secured cards convert to unsecured PNC Cash Rewards cards. The card number stays; the expiration, CVV and possibly the due date change. Certain term-change opt-outs require closing the account and paying it off.

groups.note: Legal entities involved: PNC Bank, National Association; FirstBank.

catalog_context.title: What big banks are building, and the fine print behind it
catalog_context.answer: Big banks are growing by tying checking, cards, installment loans, payments and customer data into one relationship, and using AI to approve and personalize.
catalog_context.read_first: vault:02 - Research/Banking Website Sweep — Source Document.md

catalog_context.title: Banks are moving card debt to firms willing to hold it, not forgiving it
catalog_context.answer: Big lenders are selling or buying whole debt books and moving more struggling cardholders into low-rate fixed payment plans. Very little of this is forgiveness: a sale, a charge-off or a new servicer does not wipe out what the borrower owes.
